readmeExcerpt:
# node

### Tested Distro/Env
Linux Kernel 6.8  
Ubuntu 24.04  

### Building
Using podman or docker
```
podman build --tag erlang_builder -f build.Dockerfile
./build.sh
```

### Testnet
```
#run local testnet with RPC api

#point RPC endpoint to localhost
vim /etc/hosts
127.0.0.1 nodes.amadeus.bot

#run google chrome with cert verification disabled and CORS disabled
mkdir -p /tmp/chrome_debug
google-chrome  --user-data-dir="/tmp/chrome_debug" --no-first-run --no-default-browser-check \
--ignore-certificate-errors --disable-web-security --unsafely-treat-insecure-origin-as-secure=https://nodes.amadeus.bot

#allow listening on port 80 and 443
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start=80

#run the local testnet
TESTNET=true WORKFOLDER=/tmp/testnet HTTP_IPV4=127.0.0.1 HTTP_PORT=80  ./amadeusd

# inside REPL submit a transfer to self
pk = Application.fetch_env!(:ama, :trainer_pk)
sk = Application.fetch_env!(:ama, :trainer_sk)
Testnet.call(sk, "Coin", "transfer", [pk,"1","AMA"])

# Deploy contract (default account is :trainer_pk)

pk = Application.fetch_env!(:ama, :trainer_pk)
sk = Application.fetch_env!(:ama, :trainer_sk)
Testnet.deploy "/home/user/project/node/contract_samples/assemblyscript/counter.wasm"
Testnet.call sk, pk, "get", []
Testnet.call sk, pk, "increment", ["2"]
```

### AutoUpdates + Running as a systemd service

```
cat <<EOT > /etc/sysctl.conf
#buff up the UDP stack for 1gbps
net.core.wmem_max = 268435456
net.core.rmem_default = 212992
net.core.rmem_max = 268435456
net.core.netdev_max_backlog = 300000
net.core.optmem_max = 16777216
net.ipv4.udp_mem = 3060432 4080578 6120864

# for normal networks: block spoofed UDP packets
net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter=1
net.ipv4.conf.default.rp_filter=1
EOT
```

```
cat <<EOT > /etc/security/limits.conf
root hard nofile 1048576
root soft nofile 1048576
* hard nofile 1048576
* soft nofile 1048576
root hard nproc unlimited
root soft nproc unlimited
* hard nproc unlimited
* soft nproc unlimited
root hard memlock unlimited
root soft memlock unlimited
* hard memlock unlimited
* soft memlock unlimited
EOT
cat <<EOT > /etc/systemd/system.conf
[Manager]
DefaultTasksMax=infinity
DefaultLimitNOFILE=infinity
DefaultLimitNPROC=infinity
DefaultLimitMEMLOCK=infinity
DefaultLimitLOCKS=infinity
EOT
cat <<EOT > /etc/systemd/user.conf
[Manager]
DefaultTasksMax=infinity
DefaultLimitNOFILE=infinity
DefaultLimitNPROC=infinity
DefaultLimitMEMLOCK=infinity
DefaultLimitLOCKS=infinity
EOT


cat <<EOT > /etc/systemd/system/amadeusd.service
[Unit]
Description=AmadeusD
After=network-online.target

[Service]
Type=forking
LimitNOFILE=1048576
KillMode=control-group
Restart=always
RestartSec=3
User=root
WorkingDirectory=/root/
Environment="AUTOUPDATE=true"
ExecStart=/usr/bin/screen -UdmS amadeusd bash -c './amadeusd'

[Install]
WantedBy=default.target
EOT

systemctl enable amadeusd
systemctl start amadeusd

screen -rd amadeusd
```

For non-root change:
```
WorkingDirectory=/home/youruser
User=youruser
```

```
For computor autostart
Environment="COMPUTOR=true"

For computor autostart to be validator
Environment="COMPUTOR=trainer"
```

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b9f6f596-7726-4594-81f9-d149c76ee263


  ## Major 📜

  ### 🧾 Execution claims (fork at epoch 881, height 88,100,000)
  - Validators now attest an **execution claim**: `entry_height || entry_hash || root_contractstate || root_receipts`
  (104 bytes), replacing `entry_hash || mutations_hash`
  - A consensus (≥67% aggregate signature) now certifies the block's **full state root and receipts root** — any
  contract state or receipt can be proven from it
  - Consensuses are stored and compared by **claim hash**; a node whose state root disagrees with the network halts as
  out of sync
  - The header MMR (`root_chain`) commits **claim hashes** from the fork on: one recent certificate proves every earlier
  block's claim with an MMR proof
  - `root_validator` is **dropped from block headers** after the fork — the validator set is provable from contract
  state
  - ⚠️  **Upgrade before height 88,100,000**; nodes on older versions cannot follow the chain past the fork

  ### ⚡ Faster rooting
  - Consensus signatures are verified **on arrival, in parallel**, against the epoch roster; rooting only re-checks
  quorum and masks

releases.name: v1.6.2
releases.body:
# v1.6.2

  ## Major 📜

  ### 🗳️  Stable validator slots (epoch 877)
  - Each epoch's validator set is now a **fixed roster + active mask** — a slash clears one bit instead of rewriting the list
  - Signer indexes **stay valid for the whole epoch**, even across slashes; quorum counts **active validators only**
  - Several slashes in **one block now accumulate** (previously the last one overwrote the others)
  - Aggregate signatures carry `mask_active`; `mask_size` / `mask_set_size` are **derived, no longer sent**
  - `slash_trainer` and contract `deploy` **drop their fixed 0.01 AMA exec fee** — it exceeded the 0.002 AMA exec cap, so neither could ever succeed. Metered DB/storage costs still apply
  - Slash txs **attach gas** to cover writing the new validator record

  ### 📥 Sync inbox
  - Incoming blocks, attestations and consensuses land in an **in-memory inbox (3 GB cap)**, not RocksDB
  - Signatures, hashes and txs are checked **on arrival, in parallel**; validator-set checks run only when it's the **next block to apply or root**
  - Blocks far ahead of the tip **never touch the database**; competing forks are kept until finality and **re-verified after a so

releases.name: v1.6.1 - Cheaper fees
releases.body:
# v1.6.1

## Major 📜

### ⛽ Fees ~10x cheaper (epoch 858)
- **Transact with 0.01 AMA** — each tx locks one **0.01 AMA budget** (refunded minus what it uses), down from ~1.2 AMA
- Budget covers the **history charge** + a hard **0.002 AMA exec cap** + storage with the rest
- **`attached_gas`** (optional, integer, on the call) adds budget on top for **big writes / deploys**
- A tx that can't fit its budget, or whose budget exceeds the balance, **is never included**
- History **/6**, state **/3**, DB ops + calls **/10**, WASM **1 unit per 10 ops**, **no per-tx minimum**
- Transfer: **~0.00034 AMA** (existing account), **~0.0014 AMA** (new account)

### 🔁 Faster sync, no BFT wait
- New **frontier + root loops**: fetch every missing block up to the newest tip and missing consensus, **without waiting for quorum**
- Attestations only fetched at the **live edge**; duplicate attestations are dropped before aggregation
- Peer handshakes more reliable: ANR re-signed every **3 min**, accepted up to **10 min** old

### 📨 TX relay
- Stuck txs (6s unmined) are **re-sent to the upcoming block producer** — lowest pending nonce per address only

aiSummary.oneLiner: A high-performance node implementation for the Amadeus Protocol testnet.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: The amadeusprotocol/node repository contains the reference implementation of a network node for the Amadeus Protocol, written in Rust. It provides the core infrastructure necessary to participate in the protocol's testnet, handling network communications, state synchronization, and transaction processing. The software includes built-in RPC capabilities and support for deploying and interacting with WebAssembly-based smart contracts. The node is heavily optimized for performance, utilizing system-level configurations to maximize UDP throughput and manage massive concurrent connections. It represents an experimental platform for researching high-throughput decentralized networks.
keyFeatures: Rust Implementation: Built in Rust to ensure high performance, memory safety, and efficient concurrency for network operations.
WASM Smart Contracts: Supports deploying and calling WebAssembly-based smart contracts directly on the testnet infrastructure.
Integrated RPC API: Exposes an RPC interface for querying state, submitting transactions, and managing the node programmatically.
System Tuning Scripts: Includes configuration scripts to heavily optimize the Linux network stack and system limits for maximum throughput.
Testnet Readiness: Provides out-of-the-box support for connecting to the Amadeus testnet and participating as a validator or trainer.
